section: E-governance - models, types of interaction, National e-Governance Plan, Digital India and governance outcomes
subsections: National e-Governance Plan 2006 - approval, Mission Mode Projects, vision, e-Kranti
Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims
AP e-governance initiatives - purpose and developer
E-governance awards and conferences - NCeG host city, national awards

accepted.s: The National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) was formulated by which of the following combination of organisations?
accepted.x: The National e-Governance Plan was formulated by DeitY, now MeitY, in association with DARPG.
accepted.tq: Identify the agencies directly associated with formulation rather than implementation.
accepted.sec: National e-Governance Plan 2006 - approval, Mission Mode Projects, vision, e-Kranti  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the original structure of the National e-Governance Plan, consider the following statements:
1. It consisted of 27 Mission Mode Projects and 10 components.
2. The Mission Mode Projects were divided into 9 Central, 11 State and 7 Integrated projects.
3. The original plan contained 44 Mission Mode Projects.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The original NeGP contained 27 MMPs and 10 components, divided into 9 Central, 11 State and 7 Integrated projects. The figure of 44 relates to e-Kranti, not the original plan.
accepted.tq: Separate the original structure from the later expanded figures.
accepted.sec: National e-Governance Plan 2006 - approval, Mission Mode Projects, vision, e-Kranti  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as core infrastructure of the National e-Governance Plan?
accepted.x: State Data Centres, SWAN and village-level Common Service Centres formed the core infrastructure of NeGP. The National Investment and Infrastructure Fund is unrelated to this framework.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated institutional component among the three stated infrastructure pillars.
accepted.sec: National e-Governance Plan 2006 - approval, Mission Mode Projects, vision, e-Kranti  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an Integrated Mission Mode Project under the National e-Governance Plan?
accepted.x: e-Courts is identified as an Integrated MMP. e-Panchayat is an MMP, while IT for Jobs and Early Harvest Programmes are Digital India pillars.
accepted.tq: Use the category distinction between NeGP MMPs and Digital India pillars.
accepted.sec: National e-Governance Plan 2006 - approval, Mission Mode Projects, vision, e-Kranti  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: National Portal — Digital India vision area
accepted.x: e-Panchayat is an identified Mission Mode Project under NeGP. e-Courts, e-Procurement and the National Portal are cited as Integrated MMPs.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair and distinguish MMPs from vision areas and pillars.
accepted.sec: National e-Governance Plan 2006 - approval, Mission Mode Projects, vision, e-Kranti  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly compares NeGP 1.0 and e-Kranti?
o: NeGP 1.0 had 27 MMPs, whereas e-Kranti had 44 MMPs.
NeGP 1.0 had 44 MMPs, whereas e-Kranti had 27 MMPs.
accepted.x: NeGP 1.0 had 27 MMPs, while e-Kranti, or NeGP 2.0, had 44 MMPs.
accepted.tq: Split the options by matching each figure to the correct phase.
accepted.sec: National e-Governance Plan 2006 - approval, Mission Mode Projects, vision, e-Kranti  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding e-Kranti:
1. It was approved in 2015.
2. It is a pillar of Digital India.
3. Its tagline is “Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance”.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe e-Kranti, which was approved in 2015, became a Digital India pillar and adopted the stated tagline.
accepted.tq: When all three statements independently align with the programme identity, select the complete combination.
accepted.sec: National e-Governance Plan 2006 - approval, Mission Mode Projects, vision, e-Kranti  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following represents the correct sequence of the major milestones?
A. Approval of NeGP
B. Approval of e-Kranti
C. Launch of Digital India
D. Completion of ten years of Digital India
accepted.x: NeGP was approved in 2006, Digital India was launched in 2015, e-Kranti was approved in 2015, and Digital India completed ten years in 2025. Therefore, among the given alternatives, A, C, B, D is the intended chronological order based on the stated dates.
accepted.tq: Arrange the dated milestones first and distinguish the two events occurring in 2015.
accepted.sec: National e-Governance Plan 2006 - approval, Mission Mode Projects, vision, e-Kranti  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Digital India was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on:
accepted.x: Digital India was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 1 July 2015.
accepted.tq: Use the exact launch date rather than the approval date of NeGP.
accepted.sec: Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which ministry coordinates the Digital India programme?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
accepted.x: The Digital India programme is coordinated by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, or MeitY.
accepted.tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” test to identify the nodal ministry.
accepted.sec: Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to implementation of Digital India, consider the following statements:
1. It is implemented by the whole government.
2. Public-private partnership is preferred wherever feasible.
3. Its implementation is confined to MeitY alone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Digital India is implemented across the whole government, with PPP preferred wherever feasible. It is not confined to MeitY alone.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute institutional claim that assigns a whole-of-government programme to one ministry.
accepted.sec: Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The expression “IT + IT = IT” associated with Digital India refers to:
o: Internet Technology plus Information Transfer equals Inclusive Technology
Indian Telecom plus Information Technology equals Industrial Transformation
Information Technology plus Indian Talent equals India Tomorrow
Information Transfer plus Indian Training equals Information Transparency
accepted.x: The Digital India expression “IT + IT = IT” is expanded as Information Technology plus Indian Talent equals India Tomorrow.
accepted.tq: Test the exact expansion of a slogan rather than its general policy meaning.
accepted.sec: Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal aim of Digital India is to transform India into a:
o: Digitally empowered society and knowledge economy
Centralised administrative state and industrial economy
Fully privatised economy and cashless market
accepted.x: Digital India aims to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise paired formulation used for the programme’s overarching aim.
accepted.sec: Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three vision areas of Digital India?
o: Universal conversion of all private enterprises into public enterprises
Digital infrastructure as a core utility to every citizen
accepted.x: The three vision areas are digital infrastructure as a core utility, governance and services on demand, and digital empowerment of citizens.
accepted.tq: Look for the option outside the programme’s three-part vision framework.
accepted.sec: Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Universal digital literacy, documents on the cloud and services in Indian languages are associated with which vision area of Digital India?
o: Digital infrastructure as a core utility
accepted.x: These measures are components of the vision area called digital empowerment of citizens.
accepted.tq: Match concrete features to the correct broad vision area.
accepted.sec: Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the fourth pillar of Digital India?
accepted.x: The fourth pillar is e-Governance: reforming government through technology.
accepted.tq: Use the numbered pillar sequence to distinguish adjacent pillars.
accepted.sec: Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Digital India pillar)
A. Broadband Highways
B. Universal Access to Mobile/Phones
C. Public Internet Access Programme
D. Information for All

List-II (Pillar number)
1. 1
2. 2
3. 3
4. 6

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Broadband Highways, Universal Access to Mobile/Phones, Public Internet Access Programme and Information for All are pillars 1, 2, 3 and 6 respectively.
accepted.tq: Start from the first three sequential pillars and verify the non-adjacent sixth pillar.
accepted.sec: Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Early Harvest Programmes is the ninth pillar, not the seventh. The seventh pillar is Electronics Manufacturing: target net zero imports.
accepted.tq: Check the pillar number against the official sequence.
accepted.sec: Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The target of “net zero imports” is associated with which Digital India pillar?
accepted.x: The seventh pillar, Electronics Manufacturing, carries the target of net zero imports.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive policy target to its pillar.
accepted.sec: Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is included among the sub-schemes of Digital India?
accepted.x: Electronic Governance, National Knowledge Network, Cyber Security and the IndiaAI Mission are included among the stated Digital India sub-schemes.
accepted.tq: Select the technology-oriented sub-scheme from nearby government programmes.
accepted.sec: Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Digital India completed ten years in:
accepted.x: Digital India was launched in 2015 and completed ten years in 2025.
accepted.tq: Calculate the milestone year from the launch year and confirm the stated figure.
accepted.sec: Digital India - launch, ministry, nine pillars, aims  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Andhra Pradesh initiative, started in 1998, computerised property registration?
accepted.x: CARD, or Computer-aided Administration of Registration Department, was started in 1998 for computerised property registration.
accepted.tq: Match the year and specialised administrative function to the initiative.
accepted.sec: AP e-governance initiatives - purpose and developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The primary purpose of e-Procurement in Andhra Pradesh was to:
o: Register births and deaths through village offices
Conduct online tendering and help stop collusion
Monitor consumer grievances at the national level
accepted.x: The e-Procurement initiative, introduced in 2003, enabled online tendering with the objective of stopping collusion.
accepted.tq: Infer the governance outcome from the service mechanism described.
accepted.sec: AP e-governance initiatives - purpose and developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: eSeva was introduced in 2001 as an integrated citizen service centre system for bills and certificates. The other pairs incorrectly interchange the years and purposes of the initiatives.
accepted.tq: Use both the date and the service purpose to detect swapped pairs.
accepted.sec: AP e-governance initiatives - purpose and developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: MeeSeva, meaning “At your service”, was introduced in Andhra Pradesh in:
accepted.x: MeeSeva was introduced in 2011 as a single-window G2C service centre initiative.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the later single-window service initiative from earlier eSeva and CARD projects.
accepted.sec: AP e-governance initiatives - purpose and developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Prajavani is best described as a:
o: Real-time command centre using satellite imagery alone
Web-based system for receipt, reply and monitoring of grievances at District Collectorates
accepted.x: Prajavani is a web-based system for receiving, replying to and monitoring grievances at District Collectorates.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact administrative function rather than the technology used by another platform.
accepted.sec: AP e-governance initiatives - purpose and developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Andhra Pradesh platform is associated with artificial intelligence, Big Data, GIS, IoT, real-time dashboards and a Command & Control Centre?
accepted.x: The Real Time Governance Society, or RTGS, is associated with these technologies and the Command & Control Centre.
accepted.tq: Match the cluster of advanced technologies to the specialised platform.
accepted.sec: AP e-governance initiatives - purpose and developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Real Time Governance Society of Andhra Pradesh:
1. It was established in 2017.
2. It uses a Data Lake and real-time dashboards.
3. It is described as Andhra Pradesh’s flagship digital-governance platform.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct descriptions of RTGS, established in 2017 as a flagship digital-governance platform of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Verify the date, technological features and institutional description together.
accepted.sec: AP e-governance initiatives - purpose and developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The objective of e-Pragati is most closely associated with:
o: A unified state service portal and state enterprise architecture
A network limited to district treasuries
accepted.x: e-Pragati is a unified state service portal and state enterprise architecture. It aims at faceless, paperless and cashless governance.
accepted.tq: Match the broad architecture-level function with the appropriate state initiative.
accepted.sec: AP e-governance initiatives - purpose and developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which phrase correctly describes the additional orientation of e-Pragati?
accepted.x: e-Pragati aims at faceless, paperless and cashless governance, with additional citizen services integrated into the platform.
accepted.tq: Test the exact three-part formulation associated with the initiative.
accepted.sec: AP e-governance initiatives - purpose and developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Awards for e-Governance were instituted by:
o: DARPG under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
MeitY under the Ministry of Finance
Department of Telecommunications under the Ministry of Communications
NITI Aayog under the Ministry of Home Affairs
accepted.x: The National Awards for e-Governance were instituted by DARPG under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct administrative department and parent ministry together.
accepted.sec: E-governance awards and conferences - NCeG host city, national awards  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Awards for e-Governance were started in:
accepted.x: The National Awards for e-Governance were started in 2003.
accepted.tq: Separate the awards’ starting year from the approval year of NeGP and launch year of Digital India.
accepted.sec: E-governance awards and conferences - NCeG host city, national awards  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Awards for e-Governance are presented at the:
accepted.x: The National Awards for e-Governance are presented at the National Conference on e-Governance.
accepted.tq: Match the award ceremony with its established conference platform.
accepted.sec: E-governance awards and conferences - NCeG host city, national awards  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 28th National Conference on e-Governance in 2025 was held at:
accepted.x: The 28th NCeG in 2025 was held in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the 2025 host city from the 2026 host city.
accepted.sec: E-governance awards and conferences - NCeG host city, national awards  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 29th National Conference on e-Governance in 2026 was held at:
accepted.x: Jaipur in Rajasthan hosted the 29th National Conference on e-Governance in 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the conference number and year together to avoid confusing the two host cities.
accepted.sec: E-governance awards and conferences - NCeG host city, national awards  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the 28th National Conference on e-Governance?
o: Visakhapatnam Declaration — extension of NeSDA framework to low-connectivity areas
Jaipur Declaration — net zero imports in electronics
Jaipur Declaration — launch of NeGP in 2006
accepted.x: The Visakhapatnam Declaration included extending the NeSDA framework to low-connectivity areas such as Ladakh and the North-East.
accepted.tq: Link the declaration to its specific outcome rather than to an unrelated programme milestone.
accepted.sec: E-governance awards and conferences - NCeG host city, national awards  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The theme of the 28th National Conference on e-Governance was:
o: Viksit Bharat: Civil Service & Digital Transformation
Viksit Bharat 2047: AI-enabled, Data-driven and Secure Digital Governance
Digital India for Universal Digital Literacy
accepted.x: The theme of the 28th NCeG in 2025 was “Viksit Bharat: Civil Service & Digital Transformation”.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the 2025 theme from the similarly worded 2026 theme and the e-Kranti tagline.
accepted.sec: E-governance awards and conferences - NCeG host city, national awards  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the 29th National Conference on e-Governance?
o: It was held in Visakhapatnam under the theme of civil service transformation.
It adopted the Visakhapatnam Declaration dealing with NeSDA extension to low-connectivity areas.
It adopted the Jaipur Declaration dealing with DPI, AI-enabled governance, cybersecurity and data governance.
It was the first conference to present the National Awards for e-Governance.
accepted.x: The 29th NCeG in Jaipur adopted the Jaipur Declaration on DPI, AI-enabled governance, cybersecurity and data governance.
accepted.tq: Separate the 2026 conference’s declaration and focus from those of the 2025 conference.
accepted.sec: E-governance awards and conferences - NCeG host city, national awards  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 2025 National Awards for e-Governance introduced, for the first time, a dedicated category for:
accepted.x: The 2025 awards, conducted with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, introduced a first-ever dedicated category for Gram Panchayats.
accepted.tq: Identify the new category and avoid substituting a broader institutional group.
accepted.sec: E-governance awards and conferences - NCeG host city, national awards  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the National Awards for e-Governance 2026, consider the following statements:
1. They recognised 17 projects in 7 categories.
2. e-Jagriti, a consumer grievance platform, received Silver in Category I.
3. Rohini Gram Panchayat of Dhule, Maharashtra received Gold.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the 2026 awards covered 17 projects in 7 categories, e-Jagriti received Silver in Category I, and Rohini Gram Panchayat received Gold.
accepted.tq: Check the count, award level and recipient separately before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: E-governance awards and conferences - NCeG host city, national awards  [APPSC]
